The body reports before/after Doctor regression results; the diagnostic-only change introduces no material authority transfer requiring separate final-effect proof. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Verified introduced change: The merge-base-to-head diff adds diagnostic classification after an unexpected lease-read failure, preserves immediate active-lease rejection, and releases coordinators before propagating the diagnostic.
Still necessary on inspected main: Main calls the read-only lease checker directly and wraps its failure in generic stop-and-retry guidance before the health flow can produce the database-specific recovery message.
Preserved-copy inspection and cleanup: The reused preflight requests preserveSourceArtifacts, opens the resulting snapshot read-only, returns after shared-state inspection for scope state, and closes the snapshot in finally. The new failure branch never grants repair admission. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Doctor checks and repairs OpenClaw’s local configuration and databases. Explicit repair first coordinates with running processes; database inspection then determines whether repair can proceed or must report recovery instructions. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Doctor repair request] --> B[Service and coordinator admission] B --> C[Read agent leases] C -->|Active lease| D[Refuse maintenance] C -->|Unexpected read failure| E[Inspect preserved database copy] E --> F[Release coordinators and report failure] C -->|No active lease| G[Continue schema checks and repair] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep one shared unreadable-state diagnostic while preserving lease rejection, database bytes, and coordinator cleanup. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, source establishes the failure path: non-SQLite shared-state bytes make repair’s lease query fail before the normal recovery diagnostic. Existing regression coverage exercises that exact case; it was not run during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Reusing preserved-copy preflight only after an unexpected lease-read failure provides the missing diagnosis without bypassing admission or duplicating database classification. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

Reviewed the data-model compatibility flag. This change does not alter a schema, migration, retained data, stored representation, or successful repair path. It only classifies a failed read-only lease query using the existing preserved-copy preflight and improves the resulting error. Both maintenance coordinators remain held, active leases still reject immediately, and the original corrupt file remains unchanged.

Compatibility proof is included in the 102 focused tests rerun on this head: `doctor-maintenance.schema-preflight.test.ts` admits supported legacy registries without changing their bytes, rejects newer canonical/custom/registered databases before repair, and retains the schema repair owner's current-store decisions. `doctor-health.test.ts` verifies live-writer rejection and successful repair after release. The unreadable-state E2E verifies the exact original bytes remain intact for both plain Doctor and repair. Exact-head CI is also green: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34179856078.

The automated review reports no introduced correctness or security finding. The filename-based data-model flag is resolved by this source inspection and existing compatibility proof; no migration or new schema is necessary.

Merged via squash.
